description: Figure 2 is a circular diagram illustrating a hierarchical taxonomy for medical ethics. The diagram consists of two concentric circles. The inner circle, which is smaller and located at the center, represents the four foundational "pillar principles" of medicine. The outer, larger circle surrounds the inner one and is divided into 26 distinct segments, each representing a category that has been clustered from a larger set of 256 detailed ethical principles. The visual structure suggests a hierarchical relationship, with the broad, foundational principles in the center and the more specific, categorized principles arranged around the periphery. The figure is described in the accompanying text as the "4P-26C-256G hierarchy," which is designed to ensure the comprehensiveness of the taxonomy.
